title: Why cybersecurity and physical AI must be governed together
gist: WEF authors argue physical autonomous AI (humanoids, robotaxis, drones) merges cybersecurity and safety so a cyberattack can become physical harm, and propose three questions leaders should ask before scaling plus actions for governments, companies and institutions.

insights.claim: Physical autonomous AI merges perception, decision-making and actuation, so errors, attacks or bad objectives can spread into the physical world before a human can intervene, dissolving the line between cybersecurity and safety.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Cyber risk now carries physical liability, affecting insurers, regulators and operators.
insights.locator: For physical autonomous AI, the decisive shift

insights.claim: Figure 02 humanoid robots have been tested at BMW's Spartanburg plant on sheet-metal tasks, and humanoids entering warehouses, factories and care pilots need testing, certification and accountability frameworks before scaling.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Humanoids are in early industrial pilots, with certification gaps.

insights.claim: Autonomous vehicles at scale depend on connectivity, HD maps, remote monitoring and over-the-air updates, each a failure or interference point, and mixed autonomous/human traffic risks are poorly understood; Waymo has expanded to multiple US markets.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Infrastructure dependencies are a risk for robotaxi scaling.

insights.claim: Drones are operating at scale and jamming, spoofing and hijacking have moved from theoretical to documented incidents, while airspace frameworks were not designed for many simultaneous autonomous agents; Rwanda's blood-product drone delivery shows positive use.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum

insights.claim: Leaders should ask whether autonomy boundaries are defined, whether a human 'in the loop' has the time, information, authority and skills to intervene, and what the safety case is under adversarial conditions including attack and loss of connectivity.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Checklist for diligence on autonomy deployments.

insights.claim: Companies should treat cybersecurity as a core engineering requirement rather than an end-stage compliance layer, and governments must update regulations written for drivers and non-networked physical systems.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Regulatory change is likely across AV, drone and robotics rules.
